question.problem:
Suppose $a=[2,\,-1,\,1]^{T},$ and $b=[3,\,0,\,2]^{T},$ and $p=6.$ Find the Minkowski distance between $a$ and $b.$

Rounded to three decimal places, ${d}_{p}(a,b)≈$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the Minkowski distance is defined as

$$
{d}_{p}(a,b)=‖a-b{‖}_{p}
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $v,$

$$
‖v{‖}_{p}={({\sum }_{i=1}^{N}|{v}_{i}{|}^{p})}^{1/p}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{6}(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{6} \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]‖}_{6} \\  & ={(|2-3{|}^{6}+|-1-0{|}^{6}+|1-2{|}^{6})}^{1/6} \\  & ={3}^{1/6} \\  & ≈1.201.\end{aligned}
$$
